conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode; ma = ema(close, maLength); atr(n) is the n-bar average true range; swingHigh(k)/swingLow(k) = k-th most recent confirmed pivot, trendLine(...) = projected line value at bar 0

candidates.name: MicroChannelBarBull
candidates.quote: Unlike a conventional channel where pullbacks are common, a micro channel progresses with no pullbacks, or rare, small pullbacks, making it an extremely tight channel.
candidates.description: Shared primitive, the simple-counter mechanization of a micro channel: a bar that does not pull back -- its low is at or above the prior bar's low (no overlap of the prior bar's low extreme).

complexity.reason: a bare two-bar comparison on fixed offsets

notes: Approximates Brooks's visual 'most bars touch or are close to the trend line' with a strict no-lower-low test; bear form mirrors with high[0] <= high[1].

candidates.name: MicroChannelRunLength
candidates.quote: A micro channel can last for 10 or more bars, and other times it will run for about 10 bars, have a small pullback, and then resume for another 10 bars or so.
candidates.description: Counter: the number of consecutive bars satisfying T16-01, reset to 0 on the first bar that violates it. A confirmed micro channel exists once the count reaches minBars.
candidates.pseudocode: count = number of consecutive i starting at 0 with low[i] >= low[i+1]; isMicroChannel = count >= minBars

complexity.reason: a run-length counter over a single fixed per-bar test

candidates.name: MicroChannelBreakoutBar
candidates.quote: Eventually one of the bars penetrates through the trend line or the trend channel line, creating a breakout.
candidates.description: The first bar after a confirmed micro channel whose low breaks below the prior bar's low (violating T16-01).

complexity.reason: single comparison against a persisted counter's threshold

candidates.name: High1BuyOnFailedMicroChannelBreakout
candidates.quote: They will be eager to buy below the fifth bar and above the high of the pullback bar, which is a failed breakout buy signal bar (a high 1 buy setup).
candidates.description: After a bull micro channel breaks (T16-03), buy when a later bar within maxWaitBars closes above the breakout bar's high -- the failed-breakout / high 1 buy.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the breakout bar's high (mechanized: close above it, then next bar open)

complexity.reason: needs the breakout bar's high held as persisted state across an unknown number of following bars

candidates.name: ShallowPullbackBuyDuringMicroChannel
candidates.quote: If the biggest pullback in the micro channel has been five ticks, they will place limit orders to buy any three- or four-tick pullback.
candidates.description: While a bull micro channel is confirmed, buy when a bar dips below the prior bar's low by no more than dipTicks -- a pullback shallower than the channel's own history.
candidates.pseudocode: MicroChannelRunLength[1] >= minBars && low[0] < low[1] && low[0] >= low[1] - dipTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: limit order 1-2 ticks below the low of the prior bar

complexity.reason: adds one tick-tolerance comparison to the breakout test

candidates.name: BuyCloseOfEveryBullBarInMicroChannel
candidates.quote: These traders will try to copy what the computers are doing and will buy every bull close.
candidates.description: While a bull micro channel is confirmed, buy at the close of every bull bar (aggressive continuous add-on).
candidates.book_order_type: market at the close of the bar

complexity.reason: single-bar test gated on the persisted run counter

candidates.name: MicroChannelClimaxAge
candidates.quote: When a micro trend line extends for about 10 or more bars, the odds increase substantially that there will soon be a tradable reversal. This type of trend is unsustainable and therefore a type of climax.
candidates.description: Once MicroChannelRunLength reaches climaxBars, expect an imminent breakout/reversal: favor the with-trend breakout-pullback entry (T16-04) over adding more (T16-06), and be ready for a genuine reversal rather than assuming every breakout fails.

complexity.reason: a plain threshold on the existing run-length counter

candidates.name: MicroTrendLine
candidates.quote: A micro trend line is a trend line on any time frame that is drawn across from 2 to about 10 bars where most of the bars touch or are close to the trend line.
candidates.description: A short trend line drawn through two touch points within the last microLineBars bars, reusing the general swing-pivot/line-projection machinery at a short lookback and a lower pivot strength than a full trend line.
candidates.pseudocode: p1 = swingLow(2, pivotStrength); p2 = swingLow(1, pivotStrength); require p2.bar - p1.bar <= microLineBars; slope = (p2.price - p1.price) / (p2.bar - p1.bar); microTrendLine[0] = p2.price + slope * (0 - p2.bar)

complexity.reason: swing-pivot detection and line projection over a short, adaptively chosen window

notes: Distinct from T16-01/02's strict no-overlap counter: Brooks also uses a looser 'drawn through touch points, even with tiny sub-tick penetrations' trend-line definition in this chapter.

candidates.name: FailedBreakoutOfMicroTrendLineEntry
candidates.quote: Look for any bear micro trend line and then sell below the low of any bar that pokes above any bear micro trend line. Any poke through it is a setup for a failed breakout short entry.
candidates.description: Bear form: a bar's high pokes above the projected bear micro trend line; sell when the market closes back below that bar's low. Mirrored for a bull micro trend line poked below.
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop one tick below the poke bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: inherits the micro trend line's pivot/projection dependency

candidates.name: MajorTrendLineBreakSignalsTwoLeggedPullback
candidates.quote: Bar 5 broke the major trend line of the day (any trend line lasting about an hour or so is more significant), so traders would be thinking that a two-legged pullback was more likely.
candidates.description: Distinguish a break of a 'major' (longer-duration) trend line from a micro trend line break by its age; a major-line break raises the odds of a genuine two-legged pullback rather than a one-bar failed breakout, so prefer waiting for a breakout-pullback entry over fading the break itself.

complexity.reason: needs the age of the currently active trend line tracked as persistent state

notes: 12 bars is about an hour on a 5-minute chart.

candidates.name: TwoSidedDojiCountInWindow
candidates.quote: both bars 10 and 12 were doji bars in areas of other bars with tails, and therefore were signs of two-sided trading.
candidates.description: The count of doji bars in the last windowBars is at least minCount -- a sign the market is becoming two-sided; discount fresh trend-line-break countertrend signals and prefer waiting for high-probability setups when this count is high.
candidates.pseudocode: countTrue(abs(close[i] - open[i]) <= dojiFraction * (high[i] - low[i]) for i in 0..windowBars-1) >= minCount

complexity.reason: window count of a single-bar classification

candidates.name: ExitOnMicroChannelBreakout
candidates.quote: Eventually one of the bars penetrates through the trend line or the trend channel line, creating a breakout.
candidates.description: Exit a with-trend position opened during a micro channel run once the channel breaks -- take the with-trend profit at the first sign the tight momentum has paused, rather than holding for a further extension.
candidates.book_order_type: market at the close of the breakout bar

complexity.reason: single comparison against the existing breakout classification

candidates.name: MicroChannelSpikeMeasuredMoveTarget
candidates.quote: When the micro channel is especially tight, it can be a spike on a higher time frame chart... it might reach a measured move target based on the height of the tight micro channel.
candidates.description: Treat the micro channel's own height (highest high minus lowest low over its run) as a spike height; target a further move of that height beyond the breakout.
candidates.pseudocode: microChannelHeight = highest(high, runLength) - lowest(low, runLength); target = breakoutLevel + heightMultiple * microChannelHeight
candidates.book_order_type: limit order at the measured move target

complexity.reason: the height is captured over a variable-length run (the persisted counter) rather than a fixed window

candidates.name: ReversalContextGatesMicroChannelFade
candidates.quote: The overall context can give a clue to which outcome is more likely. For example, if the market is in a strong bear trend and the bull micro channel is just a pullback, the odds favor that the breakout below the micro channel will be followed by more selling.
candidates.description: Whether a micro-channel breakout should be traded with the micro channel's own direction (T16-04 style) or against it (fading it as a flag in the larger trend) depends on the prevailing higher-level trend/always-in read.

complexity.reason: requires the AlwaysInLong/trend-context primitive (defined elsewhere) to resolve; Brooks explicitly says the same pattern trades opposite ways depending on context

candidates.name: SecondFailureIsHighOddsSecondEntry
candidates.quote: If the market now turns down again, you have just had bears trapped out and bulls trapped in. In general, if both sides get trapped in or out, the odds of success of the next setup increase.
candidates.description: When a breakout-pullback long (T16-09's long form, itself following a failed breakout) triggers and then fails again within a bar or two, the resulting second failure is a high-odds second-entry short.
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop below the failed long's signal bar (mechanized: next bar open)

complexity.reason: chains two opposite failed-breakout events with a persisted reference bar

rejected.quote: Ten years ago, traders saw micro channels as a sign of program trading. Now, since most trading is done by computers, it adds nothing to say that micro channels are signs of program trading, because every bar on the chart is due to program trading.
Although the vast majority of micro trend line breakouts are one- and two-legged pullbacks on the 1 minute chart, you should avoid trading off that chart because you will likely lose money.
rejected.reason: recommendation about which timeframe/chart to trade, not a bar-level condition the engine (fixed to one bar series) can act on.

rejected.quote: It would be prudent to reduce your position size to half or less, and increase your stop to 4 points and your profit target to 2 points.
rejected.reason: position sizing / manual parameter override for one unusual day, not a general bar-level condition.

chapter_summary: Chapter 16 is the densest chapter mined so far: it defines a micro channel as a run of bars with no lower low (a simple counter, T16-01/02, exactly the mechanizable core the mining brief anticipated) and builds a whole family of entries and exits on it -- the failed-breakout / high 1 buy, shallow-pullback and buy-every-close aggressive adds, a climax-age filter, and a measured-move target from the channel's own height. It also captures Brooks's second, looser 'drawn through touch points' micro trend line (T16-08) and its failed-breakout entry, a major-vs-micro line-age distinction, a two-sided-doji filter, and a chained second-failure second-entry idea. One candidate (T16-14) is graded research because whether to trade a micro-channel breakout with or against its own direction depends on the higher-level always-in read, which this chapter explicitly leaves as a judgment call.
